title: R6B reference case benchmark-options-4-11: the worked values of option 4 (more, smaller apartments) and option 11 (all programs combined) for the benchmark lot (215-16 Northern Boulevard, lot 70 of block 7334, R6B + C2-2, corner), built from two sealed readings per option plus an independent comparer per option; a value recorded ONLY where both readings agree on the same value and the same basis AND every cited section is captured in docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1; every disagreement, unresolved basis, eligibility, the owner's open meaning questions N1 (option 8) and N2 (shared housing) that option 11 touches, and every missing fact stays NOT KNOWN; with options 4 and 11 recorded the eleven-option set is complete across the reference cases; NO rule file, engine, result, capture, register entry, law-library edit or human verdict
objective: Add one new R6B reference case, benchmark-options-4-11, built from six sealed readings (option 4 = provenance -32/-33 with comparer -34; option 11 = -35/-36 with comparer -37), each file saved unchanged below a short truthful header. Record a value on the benchmark lot (recorded lot area 10,075 sq ft, administrative_record; GIS 10,387.99 display-only, never mixed) ONLY where (a) both readings of that option give it on the same value and the same basis, confirmed by that option's comparer, AND (b) every cited section is captured in docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1. Rows grouped by prefix (opt4-*, opt11-*) plus shared rows (both-readers-did-not-have, real-lot-missing-facts, options-out-of-scope). Option 11's rows that duplicate figures already recorded by M5-T184 (combination ceiling 2.40 -> 24,180 and 35 units = opt2; 2.00 -> 20,150 and 29 units = option 1) cross-cite the prior case+row in source_reference/why_applies and record ONLY option 11's distinctive content (the 35-31/23-20 greatest-single-use combination mechanic, shared-FA attribution, +4,030 bonus, 'shops/CF add no total FA', which programs may combine); no new floor-area pool is opened. Settled RECORD rows: opt4 residential FAR 2.00 (23-22, singular table), max residential FA 20,150 (2.00x10,075, 23-22 + 23-52 opening), DU factor 680 (23-52(b)), max 29 units (20,150/680=29.63->29, 23-52(b)), finding 'smaller apartments do not exceed 29' (23-52 opening+(b)), no-factor special-density not_applicable (23-52(a)(1)+12-10 special-density-areas, NB-05); opt11 single-use FARs residential 2.00 (23-22), commercial 2.00 (33-121 PLURAL tables -> quote-only + verbatim quote), CF 2.00 (24-11 PLURAL tables -> quote-only), combination ceiling standard 2.00 and qualifying 2.40 (35-31/23-20), max total FA 20,150 / 24,180 (35-31) + bonus +4,030, shared-FA pro-rata on total-less-shared (35-31/23-20), finding 'all single-use FARs 2.00 so shops/CF add no total FA' (35-31), DU 29 standard / 35 qualifying affordable (23-52(b)), 'no 680 factor for qualifying senior' (23-52(a)(2)), heights 30/45/55 std and 30/45/65 qualifying (23-432 via 35-63/35-631/35-632), setback 10 wide/15 narrow (23-433), may-combine shops(5)/CF(6)/two-buildings-one-ZL(8, 35-01)/parking(10), carve-outs 35-32/35-33/24-162 do not tighten R6B. Rows that stay NOT KNOWN: opt4 senior-eligibility (23-52(a)(2), applicant fact), opt4 conversions (A not_applicable / B not_known label divergence - comparer favors not_applicable but the two readings do not state the same label), opt4 min-dwelling-unit-size (MDL/HMC/Building Code, uncaptured), opt4 affordable-2.40/35 (not an option-4 value - option 2's path, cross-noted); opt11 final street-wall line (Reader A '8 ft wide/10 ft narrow' is partly wrong - 35-631(b) is 70% within 8 ft for BOTH classes, 10/15 are recess depths; only one reader numeric -> not jointly settled; comparer correction noted in prose not recorded), opt11 affordable+senior together (no ZR text read), opt11 shared housing (owner N2, framework pending 2027), opt11 split-lot meaning (owner N1, 77-00 uncaptured), opt11 overlay extent (76-131 uncaptured), opt11 UAP text (23-154 uncaptured, HTTP 403), opt11 full 35-31 carve-out sweep (35-34+ not swept), opt11 senior no-factor unit cap (not found), opt11 rear yard beyond 100 ft / CF 60%-interior coverage (geometry, 23-344(c) NB-03 draft); plus the shared real-lot-missing-facts. The mixed-building street-wall/height derivation path is recorded as an NB-06 draft reading (a condition on the opt11 height rows). Every quantity names exactly one of the nine measurement bases; no figure mixes bases; the recorded 10,075 (administrative_record) and the GIS 10,387.99 (gis) never appear combined; no value comes from a program run; nothing is labelled complies/buildable/optimal/feasible; agreement of two AI readings is not proof. Wire the case in with a new step-P11 module behind ONE thin entry into check.py and recompute the FOUR cross-case digests a new case moves (p7 PRIOR_ROWS_DIGEST, p8 OTHER_CASES_DIGEST, p9 PRIOR_CASES_DIGEST, and the step_p10 OTHER_CASES_DIGEST that the 5/8/9-10 case introduced) plus the literal CASE_IDS tuple, CASE_IDS/REQUIRED_BASE_IDS in lib and the README; step_p11 carries its own 'other cases byte-stable' digest.
business_reason: D-094 R007/R075/R084: the full feasibility report owes worked results for all eleven options; this records the last two (options 4 and 11), source-backed and independently agreed, as the single source the report/comparison and any later engine take their expected values from (never from program output), completing the per-option set. R102: the worked values and their per-section capture state feed the zoning-law-library option-04/option-11 pages. The sections options 4/11 rest on were captured by M3-T010 and earlier; this task is the sibling of M5-T184 (options 2/3/6/7) and the 5/8/9-10 case.

risks: RISK 1 (600-line split REQUIRED - the brief's explicit question): r6b_reference_cases_check.py is 594 lines at read HEAD 48d6587b; the 5/8/9-10 case's step-P10 wiring adds ~3 lines (1 import + step_p10.case_errors in validate_case + step_p10.reading_digest_errors in provenance_errors) -> ~597. That leaves only 3 lines of headroom (the guard FAILS any .py >= 600). Plain step-P11 thin wiring is again ~3 lines (1 import + 1 case_errors + 1 reading_digest_errors) -> 600 -> FAILS. So a split/refactor IS needed for THIS task. Minimal behavior-identical fix inside check.py: introduce one registry `CASE_MODULES = (step_p9, step_p10, step_p11)` near the step imports and replace the hard-coded per-module calls with two loops (`for _m in CASE_MODULES: errs += _m.case_errors(case_id, data)` in validate_case; `for _m in CASE_MODULES: errs += _m.reading_digest_errors()` in provenance_errors). Net: +1 import +1 tuple, loops replace the existing hard lines -> check.py ~599, < 600 but TIGHT (1 line). Because options 4/11 complete the option set, no further case is expected, so 599 is an acceptable terminal state - BUT the producer MUST confirm the real count with `python tools/modularity_check.py --check`; if it lands >= 600, extract the case-module dispatch + reading-digest aggregation into the new module r6b_reference_cases_cases.py (already in allowed_paths as a contingency; preserve public imports per CLAUDE.md principle 16) so check.py gets durable headroom, NEVER weaken the 600 guard. step_p11 itself must be < 600.

RISK 2 (plural 'tables' key): 33-121 (commercial FAR 2.00) and 24-11 (CF FAR 2.00) carry their numbers under the plural 'tables' key; the checker's table_assertion reads singular 'table' (None) and would fail 'has no table'. Record 33-121 = 2.00 and 24-11 = 2.00 as arithmetic operands / quote-only + a verbatim quote, table_assertion:null; a reviewer eyeballs the numbers against each snapshot's 'tables'. 23-22 (residential 2.00/2.40) and 23-432 (heights) carry singular 'table' -> table_assertion works. 35-31, 23-20, 23-52, 35-01, 35-63, 35-631, 35-632, 35-32, 35-33, 32-161, 23-433, 23-51, 54-311, 22-12/22-121 are prose-only -> quote-only.

RISK 3 (one case, TWO reading pairs AND TWO comparers): unlike the 5/8/9-10 case (three pairs + one shared comparer -25), this case has option 4 = -32/-33 + comparer -34 and option 11 = -35/-36 + comparer -37. The generic CASE_READINGS forces one tuple per row, so the case is NOT registered there; check.py both_readings_errors no-ops for it and step_p11 enforces the pair+comparer per row prefix (opt4 -32/-33/-34, opt11 -35/-36/-37). A negative test MUST prove a one-reading / wrong-pair / wrong-comparer row is refused.

RISK 4 (comparer is an adjudicator, not a value source): record only where both readings of an option agree on the same value and basis; the comparer only confirms agreement and resolves reader-vs-reader disputes. Keep opt4 conversions (A not_applicable / B not_known) and opt11 final street-wall line NOT KNOWN; C11 found Reader A's '8 ft wide / 10 ft narrow' partly wrong (35-631(b) = 70% within 8 ft for BOTH classes; 10/15 are recess depths) and Reader B gave no numeric row, so the two readings do not jointly settle it - the comparer's 8-ft correction is noted in prose, NEVER recorded as a value.

RISK 5 (certainty-label divergence on opt11 height applicability): Reader A 'applies' vs Reader B 'not_known (draft, NB-06)'; the comparer confirms the VALUES (30/45/55, 30/45/65) are settled and that the divergence is only the review-status. Record the height VALUES (both agree) WITH a condition that the mixed-building street-wall/height derivation path is an NB-06 draft reading awaiting review - do not record the applicability as fully settled, and do not drop the values.

RISK 6 (provenance header honesty): the six reading files end END-OF-REPORT but lack 'sealed folder' and a hard-rule marker. The producer prepends a truthful header to -32..-37 supplying the literal phrase 'sealed folder' and a distinct marker; the readers worked from the captures (option-4-A read only snapshots/NB/cases/library; option-4-B 'no ZR website fetch required'; option-11-A 'No program run was read'; both comparers reopened the v1 snapshots), so the header states each file's actual method and must NOT over-claim 'no outside access' beyond what the file supports. Digests are computed on the saved file AFTER the header.

RISK 7 (uncaptured sections convention): zero not_captured citations; 76-131, 23-154, 77-00/Art VII Ch 7, 35-34+ neighbours and MDL/HMC/Building Code are named only in the prose of not-known / both-readers-did-not-have rows, never as a value basis or a formal citation.

RISK 8 (capture-dependency + shared-file ordering): the case cites the earlier captures by content_digest and shares README.md, lib.py, check.py, render.py, test_r6b_reference_cases.py and the p7/p8/p9/p10 tests with M5-T184 and the 5/8/9-10 case. M5-T185 (5/8/9-10), M5-T184 and M3-T010 must ALL be accepted first (frozen digests / stable base). See the order note.
RISK 9 (sole reference-case task in flight): must be the ONLY open reference-case task while open; it integrates after M5-T185, M5-T184 and M3-T010 and is the last of the eleven-option cases.

RISK 10 (cross-case citation without double-recording): option 11's 20,150/29 and 24,180/35 are the SAME figures M5-T184 recorded (opt2) and option 1 settled. These rows must cross-cite the prior case+row in source_reference/why_applies and record ONLY option 11's distinctive combination mechanic; they must not open a second independent floor-area pool or contradict the prior cases (reviewer checks the numbers reproduce).
